events.title: US CPI, January 2023
events.text: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) rose 0.5 percent in January on a seasonally adjusted basis, after increasing 0.1 percent in December. Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 6.4 percent before seasonal adjustment.
events.sourceNote: BLS lead, embargo until 8:30 a.m. ET. A pre-release economist poll was not re-fetched for this row, so the naive card abstains.

events.title: US CPI, June 2023
events.text: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) rose 0.2 percent in June on a seasonally adjusted basis, after increasing 0.1 percent in May. Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 3.0 percent before seasonal adjustment.
events.sourceNote: Engine sees the BLS lead only. Naive cool-inflation card uses the Reuters poll, which is not in the engine text: 0.2% on the month and 3.0% on the year versus 0.3% and 3.1% forecast.

events.title: US CPI, October 2023
events.text: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) was unchanged in October on a seasonally adjusted basis, after increasing 0.4 percent in September. Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 3.2 percent before seasonal adjustment. The energy index fell 2.5 percent over the month.
events.sourceNote: BLS lead plus the energy sentence in the same opening. Naive card abstains: poll page not archived in this run.

events.text: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.4 percent in March on a seasonally adjusted basis, the same increase as in February. Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 3.5 percent before seasonal adjustment.
events.sourceNote: Engine sees the BLS lead only. The naive hot-inflation card uses the Reuters poll, which is not in the engine text: 0.4% on the month and 3.5% on the year versus 0.3% and 3.4% forecast.

events.title: US CPI, August 2024
events.text: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) increased 0.2 percent on a seasonally adjusted basis, the same increase as in July. Over the last 12 months, the all items index increased 2.5 percent before seasonal adjustment.

events.sourceNote: BLS lead, 8:30 a.m. ET. Naive hot-labor card is the pre-set verb rule: payrolls rose and unemployment did not.

events.title: US employment situation, January 2024

events.sourceNote: BLS lead, 8:30 a.m. ET. Naive hot-labor card: payrolls rose, unemployment did not.

Reuters poll was 175,000 payrolls versus the 114,000 print (https://www.reuters.com/markets/rates-bonds/view-soft-us-payrolls-number-opens-door-september-fed-cut-2024-08-02/). events.title: Saudi July output cut, June 2023
events.text: Saudi Arabia will make a deep cut to its output in July on top of a broader OPEC+ deal to limit supply into 2024. Saudi output would drop to 9 million barrels per day in July from around 10 million barrels per day in May.
events.sourceNote: Sunday, 4 June 2023, Vienna. Clock is the calendar day, not a minute-stamped wire. Cash session is the next SPY session. Naive oil-cut card.

events.title: OPEC+ voluntary cuts, November 2023

events.sourceNote: Reuters update 22:12 UTC on 30 November 2023, after the US cash close, so the cash reaction session is the next SPY session. Official tally: https://www.opec.org/pr-detail/39-30-nov-2023.html. Naive oil-cut card.

events.title: Tesla Q2 2024 results
events.text: Tesla reported its lowest profit margin in more than five years and missed Wall Street earnings. Automotive gross margin was 14.6 percent versus analysts' estimates of 16.3 percent. Operating income decreased to $1.6 billion, a 6.3 percent operating margin.
events.sourceNote: Reuters copy filed before the 24 July cash open (updated 07:16 UTC on 24 July) plus Tesla's own Q2 operating-income line. The later 'shares tumbled' story was not fed. Webcast was 4:30 p.m. CT on 23 July. Naive card is short TSLA, QQQ, and SPY.
